_comment: The outcomes M01's acceptance tests assert. Each row names the behaviour, the request and the exact expected status and message_key, so the fixture file and the tests cannot drift apart silently.

cases.name: business API refused before 2FA completes
cases.given: T1 has an active factor and a password-only session

cases.name: challenge is not a business session
cases.when: GET /api/v1/accounts using only the challenge id

cases.name: replayed TOTP code is refused inside its own window
cases.given: the same code accepted a moment ago
cases.why: last_accepted_step makes acceptance atomic, so a code cannot be used twice even within its 30-second step.

cases.name: concurrent reuse of one recovery code succeeds exactly once
cases.given: two simultaneous requests with the same unused code

cases.name: replaying an already-used recovery code is refused
factor reset revokes existing sessions
cases.given: T1 has two live sessions and a pending case; P1 approves it

cases.name: device-loss recovery works with no SMS service
cases.given: no SMS provider is configured or reachable anywhere in the profile

cases.name: delegation cannot exceed the delegator's scope
cases.given: an actor with roles.delegate scoped to section C1

cases.name: last active owner is protected
cases.given: O1 is the only active owner

cases.name: role removal affects evidence downloads
cases.given: an actor whose grant permitted a private file read
cases.when: the grant is removed, then the download is retried

then.note: Access checks apply to private files, not only to API routes. The decision must invalidate promptly on grant change.

cases.name: a required factor cannot be disabled on a protected role
cases.given: O1 holds the owner role, which requires 2FA
cases.when: an attempt to disable the factor

then.note: Progressive cooldown, never a permanent attacker-triggered lockout.
